title: Hot Cross Buns
hook: Three notes. A first win in the first lesson.

title: London Bridge Is Falling Down
hook: First dotted rhythm, in a tune they can already sing.

title: Mary Had a Little Lamb
hook: Four notes next to each other, and every kid knows it.

title: Row, Row, Row Your Boat
hook: First taste of 6/8, the "rocking" feel. Also works as a round.

title: This Old Man
hook: The "knick-knack paddywhack" bar is great for eighth notes.

title: Frère Jacques (Are You Sleeping?)
hook: A round: once two kids can play it, start the second one two bars later.

title: Twinkle Twinkle Little Star
hook: Same tune as the ABC song and Baa Baa Black Sheep, so it counts as three songs.

title: Old MacDonald Had a Farm
hook: The "here a moo, there a moo" bars are great fast-repeated-note practice.

title: Lightly Row
hook: The classic first "real" piece in lots of method books; five notes, two phrases.

title: Ode to Joy
hook: A real Beethoven tune with only five notes. Kids love saying they can play Beethoven.

title: Symphony No. 5 – opening riff
hook: Da-da-da-DUM: the most famous four notes in music, played high and then low.

title: Creaky Staircase (Halloween)
hook: Creeps up one key at a time, then ends on the spooky "devil's interval".

title: Gravel Road (original riff)
hook: A first riff on just a few low keys. Loop it until it grooves.

title: Pop Goes the Weasel
hook: Everyone shouts "POP!" on the high note. A fun 6/8 piece.

title: Happy Birthday to You
composer: Mildred & Patty Hill (tune "Good Morning to All", 1893)
hook: Kids get to play it at every party. The high note in bar 6 is their "big moment".

title: When the Saints Go Marching In
hook: A band favourite. Once you know it, a friend can play C, F and G chords along with you.

title: Amazing Grace
hook: A slow 3/4 melody, good for practising tone and letting notes ring.

title: Yankee Doodle
hook: Bouncy and quick; the chorus brings in dotted rhythms.

title: Oh! Susanna
hook: A bouncy banjo song; the chorus moves around C, F and G.

title: Drunken Sailor (sea shanty)
hook: Shanties are a big hit with kids. Only Dm and C, so it suits a band. Schools often sing it as "What shall we do with the grumpy pirate?"

title: Spring – opening theme
hook: Sounds fancy, but it only uses a handful of keys.

title: Canon in D – theme
hook: The wedding piece. It uses the same chord loop (D-A-Bm-F#m-G-D-G-A) as hundreds of pop songs, which is a great talking point.

title: Eine kleine Nachtmusik – opening
hook: Mozart's "rocket" opening: arpeggios that shoot upwards.

title: Lullaby (Wiegenlied)
hook: A gentle piece that everyone recognises. Good on piano.

title: Silent Night
hook: Slow and calm, good for practising letting notes ring and playing smoothly.

title: Jingle Bells (chorus)
hook: The end-of-year concert banker. Lots of repeated notes, so it's quick to learn.

title: We Wish You a Merry Christmas
hook: Bright 3/4 tune; the "good tidings" chorus is a nice contrast.

title: Joy to the World
hook: Opens with a full C major scale going down, so it doubles as scale practice.

title: Deck the Halls
hook: The "fa la la" scale run in bar 11 is sneaky scale practice.

title: Toccata in D minor – opening
hook: THE spooky organ tune. Perfect for Halloween; the same motif drops an octave each time.

title: Mars – rhythm riff in 5/4
hook: The pounding rhythm from Mars in 5/4. Count "1-2-3-4-5" and feel like a film soundtrack.

title: In the Hall of the Mountain King
hook: A sneaky tune that keeps creeping. Start on Slow and work up to Full speed.

title: Twelve-Bar Shuffle in A
hook: The rock'n'roll left-hand pattern every band player needs.

title: Ghost in the Hallway (Halloween)
hook: A slow, floaty 6/8 tune that drifts down in half-steps, like a ghost gliding past. Practise letting long notes ring.

title: Haunted Music Box (Halloween)
hook: A wonky little A-minor waltz, like a wind-up toy in an empty house. The D# notes make it sound "wrong" in the creepy way. Lovely on piano.

title: Zombie March (Halloween)
hook: A heavy D minor stomp that slides down one key at a time, like a zombie shuffling off.

title: Robot Stomp (original riff)
hook: A stop-start robot riff. The rests have to be silent, so lift your fingers!

title: Skateboard Sun (original riff)
hook: A happy, bright riff that bounces between three keys.

title: Thunder Chug (original riff)
hook: Fast repeated low notes with higher notes jumping out between. Keep your hand relaxed.

title: Für Elise – opening
hook: The piano piece every kid wants to learn.

title: Can-Can (Galop Infernal)
hook: Fast, silly and very recognisable. A good "speed challenge" piece.

title: Minuet in G
composer: Christian Petzold (from the Anna Magdalena Bach Notebook)
hook: A proper classical recital piece, good for a first concert.

title: Greensleeves
hook: A beautiful A-minor melody, also the tune of "What Child Is This". Good for expression and dotted rhythms.

title: Prelude in C (bars 1–19)
composer: J. S. Bach (Well-Tempered Clavier I, BWV 846)
hook: One finger pattern, a new chord every bar. Sounds amazing on piano, and kids can see the chords moving. Stops at the first big C-major cadence.

title: Korobeiniki
hook: Kids instantly recognise it as "the block-stacking video game song". Play it faster each round, like the game.

title: House of the Rising Sun (picking pattern)
hook: Broken chords (Am, C, D, F) rolling up and down the keys.

title: Witch's Cauldron (Halloween)
hook: A bubbling pattern (Am, F, E) that never stops stirring, like a horror-film theme.

title: Space Gallop (original riff)
hook: The metal "gallop" rhythm (da-da-dum) on the low E, climbing to G and A, then dropping through C to B. Feels like galloping horses.
